title: Optimize toolkit: onboarding handoff and visual assets for batching, caching, and quantization UI
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Create a cohesive set of onboarding visuals, annotated product screenshots, and handoff assets for the Optimize toolkit. Focus on the new batching and caching recommendations card, the quantization configuration UI (modal + details page), and two lightweight illustrated screens for the quickstart flow that explain operational trade-offs (latency vs cost). Deliverables should be ready for PM/Eng handoff and inclusion in the docs portal and in-app quickstart carousel.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with organized pages: Quickstart hero, Recommendations card variants, Quantization modal & details page, Assets & icons
Three annotated product screenshot exports (desktop & tablet): Recommendations card, Quantization modal, Quickstart step showing batch/caching toggle
Hand-off spec sheet (MD): spacing, type, token examples, copy variants for LITE/ADVANCED prompts
Ready-to-upload PNG/SVG assets for docs and in-app carousel (proper naming convention)
PM and ENG review completed with sign-off comments addressed
Design tokens and component references mapped to Redwood design system tokens
steps: 1) Audit existing quickstart imagery and identify overlaps/anti-patterns
2) Create low-fidelity wireframes for 3 core screens and get PM alignment
3) Iterate on hi-fi comps in Figma and create annotated overlays
4) Export screenshots and assets, write handoff MD with copy variants
5) Sync with ENG on implementation constraints (responsive sizes, SVG support)
6) Final review and upload to docs + assign to content owner
design_notes: Primary goal is clarity: users should immediately understand when to enable batching vs caching and the effect of quantization on latency/cost/quality. Use simple metaphors (queue icon for batching, memory cache icon for KV caching) and a two-column details modal for quantization trade-offs. Keep copy short: an explainer sentence, expected impact range (e.g., ~20-40% cost reduction), and a link to advanced docs. Prefer neutral illustrative palette aligned with Redwood brand; use green for recommended suggestions and amber for cautionary guidance.
mockups_needed: Recommendations card with A/B variants (compact vs detailed)
